content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving omeprazole and other medications. 1. Omeprazole reduces the levels of erlotinib by altering the pH of the upper gastrointestinal tract, which decreases erlotinib's solubility and bioavailability. Concomitant use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) with erlotinib is contraindicated and should be avoided whenever possible. 2. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, as strong or moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors can increase systemic exposure to mavacamten, potentially leading to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. 3. Omeprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir through an unspecified interaction mechanism, likely involving CYP2C19 inhibition and reduced gastric acidity. This coadministration is contraindicated, as it may result in loss of virologic response and resistance development. 4. Omeprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated, as it may lead to treatment failure and resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. 5. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by inhibiting CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Drugs that inhibit these enzymes can increase systemic exposure to abrocitinib and its active metabolites, potentially increasing adverse effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Omeprazole decreases the levels of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as separating doses may not eliminate the interaction due to the prolonged effect of PPIs. 7. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as coadministration with strong CYP2C19 inducers can lower exposure to CYP2C19 substrates. 8. Apalutamide also decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute another drug, as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce exposure to CYP3A4 substrates. 9. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility. Substantially reduced plasma concentrations of atazanavir are expected with PPI coadministration. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 10. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Omeprazole decreases the effects of ceritinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Omeprazole decreases the effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which is essential for converting clopidogrel into its active metabolite. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction may reduce clopidogrel's efficacy in inhibiting platelet aggregation. 14. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of dacomitinib through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as PPIs decrease dacomitinib concentrations, potentially reducing its efficacy. 15. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of digoxin by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as coadministration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors has not been studied and may increase adverse effects. 19. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction may increase the risk of adverse effects. 20. Fluvoxamine increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 22. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as coadministration with weak CYP3A inhibitors may require dose adjustments. 27. Omeprazole decreases the effects of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to sustained-release dosage forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration with drugs that raise gastric pH, and consider using short-acting antacids instead of PPIs or H2 antagonists. 31. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Omeprazole may cause a hyperresponse in gastrin secretion during secretin stimulation testing, potentially leading to a false diagnosis of gastrinoma. Temporarily discontinue omeprazole at least 14 days before testing to allow gastrin levels to return to baseline. 36. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases. Avoid coadministration with PPIs, or administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. 37. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
